verdict.rationale: Hyperbrowser's docs describe HyperAgent, its first-party AI browser-automation framework, as open-source, and its MCP server is published on GitHub, so some first-party source is readable. However, the core managed cloud-browser platform (sessions, stealth, scrape/crawl APIs, sandboxes) shows no evidence of open source, and no specific license is named. Missing for 10: open source for the core platform, a named open license (e.g., MIT/Apache), and confirmation of the HyperAgent repository and its license terms.
